{"concepts_used":["GC-0128","GC-0040","GC-0116","GC-0117","GC-0046","GC-0097","GC-0104","GC-0124","GC-0113","GC-0135"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part52/2/2/1","quote":"Matters arising under the Act in which the Registrar is required to make a decision which will determine the rights of one of the parties involved relative to another party are referred to as “inter partes” matters."},{"ref":"TMM/Part52/2/2/1","quote":"Both of the interested parties have the opportunity to be heard before the decision is made, and the hearing is referred to as an inter partes hearing."},{"ref":"TMM/Part52/2/2/1","quote":"These include oppositions to registration of trade marks under section 52, oppositions under section 96 to applications for removal for non-use, and oppositions to extensions of time under section 224 which are for a period greater than three months."},{"ref":"TMM/Part55/2#1","quote":"The legislation provides that the following actions may be opposed: Amendment of a trade mark application (s 65A) Registration of another party’s trade mark (s 52) Protection of an International Registration Designating Australia held by another party (reg 17A.33) Removal of a registered trade mark for non-use (s 96) Cessation of protection of a Protected International Trade Mark for non-use (reg 17A.48D) Grant of an extension of time of more than three months (s 224)."},{"ref":"TMM/Part52/3#1","quote":"In opposition matters, where the Registrar has allowed a reasonable time for all parties to indicate whether they wish to be heard, or where all parties indicate that they do not wish to be heard - per paragraph 21.15(5)(a) - the Registrar is not required to hold a hearing."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s203","quote":"The Registrar may not exercise a power under this Act in any way that adversely affects a person applying for the exercise of that power without first giving that person a reasonable opportunity of being heard."}],"answer":"**Manual practice — who gets to be heard?**
An *inter partes* matter is one in which the Registrar’s decision determines one party’s rights relative to another party. **Both interested parties have an opportunity to be heard before the decision is made**, not just the party seeking the Registrar’s action. [TMM/Part52/2/2/1]

**Manual practice — what proceedings are included?**
The Manual expressly identifies:
- oppositions to registration of trade marks (s 52);
- oppositions to applications for removal for non-use (s 96); and
- oppositions to extensions of time exceeding three months (s 224). [TMM/Part52/2/2/1]

Its broader list of actions that may be opposed also includes amendment of a trade mark application (s 65A), protection of an International Registration Designating Australia (reg 17A.33), and cessation of protection of a protected international trade mark for non-use (reg 17A.48D). These are additional opposition proceedings identified by the Manual. [TMM/Part55/2#1]

**An opportunity does not necessarily mean a hearing must occur.** The Manual says that, in opposition matters, a hearing is not required where the Registrar has allowed a reasonable time for all parties to indicate whether they wish to be heard, or all parties indicate that they do not wish to be heard. [TMM/Part52/3#1]

**Act — separate general safeguard:** Section 203 prohibits the Registrar from exercising a power adversely to a person applying for its exercise without first giving that person a reasonable opportunity to be heard. [TMA1995/s203]

The opposition-specific statutory references above are reported from the **Manual**, not independently verified against supplied Act or Regulations extracts; those provisions themselves were not supplied."}
